commits.message:
Derive fault-proof step lists from the core deployment members

Core's deploymentFamilyStepNames already owns every family's ordered step
contract names, but fault-proofs restated them by hand. The deployment
entries table (447 lines) is now derived from core in catalogue order. The
ten older families whose resolution checks only their first step stay
that way, named once in FIRST_STEP_ONLY_DEPLOYMENT_CATEGORIES instead of
being implied by a shorter literal; the removal-deployment test support
uses that set instead of a catalogue-position rule.

Cursor family definitions take their step contract names from core through
cursorStepContractNames, and the linear family specs from core by category;
both refuse at load when core's step count differs from the spec's. The
hand-written records for double spend, missing signature, value not
preserved, network id and the fabricated CLI contracts read core too.

The always-succeeds chains in the node service and the fault-proofs
emulator are sized from core instead of 100 hard-coded counts;
validationTraceDispute keeps its one-step scaffold as an explicit override.
Every derived list was checked equal to the one it replaces.

Collapse per-family fault-proof wiring onto the shared registry

Thirteen families hand-copied the manifest-bound run-or-resume body; they
now alias the shared runOrResumeManifestBoundFamilyWorkflow like the other
sixteen. Nine per-family cancel wrappers used only by tests are deleted, so
own-thread reclaim and the tests share submitLinearFaultCancel.

The SDK's per-category *_FRAUD_CATEGORY_ID aliases are deleted; callers read
FRAUD_PROOF_CATALOGUE_CATEGORY_IDS. The category-label switch becomes a
camelCase-to-kebab rule with one override, equal for all 52 categories.
FAMILY_DEFINITIONS and CURSOR_FAMILY_DEFINITIONS, read only by tests, are
deleted; the tests and the family checklist read definitions from the
family application registry instead.

Witness roles are built from three nested shared sets (core, chunked
verify, membership) instead of 46 restated lists, in the same order. The
adapter registration rows are derived from the catalogue order with a
default reason; their output is byte-identical.

Test validation-worker startup retries through the real node startup

The test replaced the DA startup sequence and the L1 follower with counters
and took a started follower as proof the node started. Since the follower
starts inside that sequence, the proof never came. It now runs the real
startup with the real pool and worker, and reads the outcome from the node
itself: readiness held at local_preflight once the workers are up, or the
validation_workers failure with its reason and attempt count.

Attach a second operator before the stack's first block

A node with an empty database builds its ledger only from the deployment's
genesis, so it cannot join once a block has committed. The twin and
rehearsal flows now run the stack with --setup-only, attach operator-2,
then run the journeys. The readiness list records late join (#868) as
after-launch work.

Start following L1 before the startup DA checks read through the follower

The node's L1 reader answers a protocol address only from the follower's
facts, but the startup DA checks read the on-chain DA threshold before
the follower started. On a fresh database there is no follower cursor
yet, so the read could never succeed: the node waited out its startup
budget, exited and restarted forever.

Startup now follows L1 to the node's tip first, then runs the DA checks,
still before any DA publication, block production or other duty. The
follower may resend transactions an earlier run journaled before the
checks pass; a resend publishes nothing to DA.

The test that replaced the whole startup sequence with a stub no longer
reaches the follower and is deleted; the new test runs the real sequence
on a fresh database.

Share the follower's queue, genesis and slot-config code across roles

The DA committee decoded state-queue outputs and walked the landed queue
with its own copies of the SDK decoder and the follower's linked-queue walk.
It now calls both; the walk keeps the committee's invalid_output detail.
The slot-config cache written four times over (node provider, node ledger
access, committee follower, watcher follower) is one cache on the ledger
provider that forgets a failed read.

The watcher read its genesis identity with a reader of its own and a
separate chainSync.genesisConfigPath setting checked against the node
config's path. It now uses the shared readNativeLedgerGenesis, which gains
the watcher's strictness for both roles: a repeated JSON key is refused and
the genesis file is read through a canonical path. The setting is gone from
the watcher config and every in-repo producer; the acceptance config binds
the genesis by digest instead.

The watcher's state-queue observation table had no reader since #798; its
store and table creation are deleted, and an existing database keeps the
unused table without a migration. The native block admission and exact
chain-sync record modules, and the follower's Kupmios subclass, were used
only by devnet tooling and move into midgard-node-tools.

The devnet journal's hand-rolled durable write becomes a synchronous
variant of core's atomic write: exact file mode, a no-collision temp name,
a full write loop and a sync of every directory it creates.

Read an attached operator's wallets through the stack's Kupo and Ogmios

A second instance runs no Kupo or Ogmios of its own, but its host tools
built their L1 endpoints from its own port settings, so its wallet check
reached nothing and the run stopped before attaching. The attached
instance now takes the stack's KUPO_PORT and OGMIOS_PORT.
Record the owner's confirmation of the DA slash grace and pool floor

Refresh the public testnet readiness review at 2ad2f8418

Every implementation item now cites the merge it landed in. The dated
schedule becomes the remaining ordered steps, since the full P1 scope
ships and dates move. Release gates record the rulings since 10-13 and
mark what this review could not confirm as Unverified. R6 states what the
fast-timer twin has and has not covered.

Gate every runnable golden channel in CI

Four golden channels had a --check mode but no workflow step, so preflight
reported them warn-only and a stale vector could not turn CI red: the V1
transaction root, the RejectionReasonV1 vectors, the native-transaction
compact constants and the CEK large-integer program fixture. Run each by id
in the golden-channels job.

The CI wiring test now also checks the other direction: every warn-only
check in the registry must be listed with the reason it is not gated, so a
new channel left out of CI fails the test instead of going quietly
warn-only. The Haskell script-decode channel stays listed, since CI builds
no probe for it.

Import detectors from detection-only modules so fault-proofs modules load in any order

The complete-replay detection union imported three families' detectors
through their workflow modules, which import the orchestrator, which
imports the union. That closed a 58-module import cycle, and which module
was evaluated first decided whether WITNESS_ROLES and the script-decode
auxiliary reference scripts were defined yet when read at load time.

The union now imports each detector from its detection-only module. The
field-item-width detector and its violation id move into
field-item-width-illegal/replay.ts, and the order-only family imports in
complete-replay.ts are removed.

module-evaluation-order.test.ts imports every module still on a cycle
first, in a fresh module runner, and requires the package exports to
match a reference import.

Refs #866

Back the devnet DA bond pool once, from a committee member

The devnet topped up the DA committee's bond pool to its full bond on
every service start, paying from the operator's main wallet. That hid a
slash behind the next restart, and the dedicated-payer check refuses the
operator's wallet as payer, so a fresh devnet could not back its pool.

The pool is now backed once, on the deployment's first start, from the
DA cosigner's wallet: a committee member's wallet that no running
service spends. The journal records the backing. A later start that
finds the pool below its bond reports it and leaves the top-up to a DA
operator running `da-bond top-up`.

Report a merged transfer as finalized again

Transaction status compared the merge-finalization job's payload against
a field the job stopped writing when merges moved to deltas, so no
transaction could ever report a finalized merge. The job id already names
the header, and the job starts only once the header's root matches its
journal, so the status read no longer re-reads the payload.

The test now seeds the job the way the merge writes it.

Give emulator tests the node's production index

The follower provider no longer scans the ledger for an address outside
its tracked scope, which exposed test hosts that tracked less than a node
does. The shared follower host can now take the node's configuration and
track its own wallets as production does; the operator-inactivity and
reserve-payout fixtures build the node's production index; the empty
wallet tests declare their wallet as the node's own; and the DA bond test
checks its fresh address on the emulator's ledger directly.
Read the harness node command past a leading --l1 access in the runbook check
